title: Mixing socially with the musicians and the Harmony Inn
summary: They never ate with the musicians but visited homes and parties, nervously, and recall a large club where Emile Barnes played.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Did you ever eat a meal with the musicians?
I don't... No, I don't think so. I think it was almost out of the question.
As we went to their homes.

They would have invited us to their homes, too. We weren't cooking much. Well, I can remember being very nervous around the corner when we'd go to those parties. Yeah. Nobody was supposed to find out that we were mingling. That's right. I think we felt rather brave about all that. At the same time, we were nervous.
Yeah. I felt a little scared about all that.
Yeah. Well, you could have been kicked out of medical school if... Oh, I doubt it, yes. I think not. Yeah. I think Kit Howard was playing with Emil Barnes again. It seems to me that...

Mm-hmm. And I did... You and I and Greenwood and somebody else went down to a... Oh, a club downtown somewhere. Kind of a cavernous sort of a place. Not... Mm-hmm. Not small... Not... Much larger dance floor than Luggan's. Did you ever go to the Harmony Inn?
I don't know. It's down. I think it means you can play by now. But... It was such a big place, and Emil Barnes played that, but I don't know that that's where it was around.
Well, it could have been. Yeah. It was bigger than Luggan, you know. Yeah. It wasn't fast, but it was bigger.
